title: White House Asks Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle to Resign Over Misconduct Reports
excerpt: New press secretary Katie Zacharia announced the ouster at her first briefing; Trump said he 'didn't like what I read,' while Guilfoyle denies the allegations.
body:
• The White House has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as US ambassador to Greece, new press secretary Katie Zacharia announced at her first briefing on Tuesday.
  • President Trump confirmed the move, saying of the reports about Guilfoyle: "I didn't like what I read."
  • Wall Street Journal reporting alleged she asked a donor to pay a $100,000 credit card bill before her confirmation and accepted lavish gifts in Athens — allegations her lawyers dispute.
  • Guilfoyle, ambassador since September 2025 and formerly engaged to Donald Trump Jr., said the allegations are false and she will defend her reputation.

The White House has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as US ambassador to Greece, ending the tenure of one of the most recognisable figures in President Donald Trump's movement after a string of reports alleging misconduct in Athens and before she took up the post.

New press secretary Katie Zacharia confirmed the decision at her first briefing on Tuesday. "We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign. She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well," Zacharia said, according to CNN and USA Today. Trump, asked about the move later, was blunter: "I didn't like what I read," he said, adding that he had not spoken to Guilfoyle personally.

The allegations

The dismissal follows Wall Street Journal reporting that Trump campaign donor Eric Deters said Guilfoyle pressed him, days before her Senate confirmation hearing last year, to pay off a $100,000 American Express bill, suggesting she would be his ally inside the administration if he did. Deters told CNN there was "no question it was a quid pro quo"; he did not send the money. Guilfoyle's lawyers dispute the authenticity of the messages attributed to her and say Deters owed her money for speeches and consulting work done before her nomination.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=izY7HS5msVQ

Further reports alleged that she accepted lavish gifts as ambassador and brought a lobbyist for a Greek construction company into official meetings. Her lawyers have denied the claims about soliciting money, described reporting on her travel as misleading, and said she complied with federal gift and reporting rules.

"These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity."

— Kimberly Guilfoyle, in a statement on X

A rapid fall

Guilfoyle's ouster is a sharp reversal for a former Fox News host who spent four years engaged to the president's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., and remained inside the family's political circle after their split. Trump had publicly weighed the decision on Monday, telling reporters, "Well, we're looking at it. Yeah, we're not happy." CNN reported that Guilfoyle had spent the weekend rallying support among administration officials and had been reluctant to resign.

In a lengthy post on X shortly after the briefing, she acknowledged her time as ambassador "may be coming to an end" while disputing the allegations. "While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end," she wrote.

What's next

The White House has not named a successor or said when Guilfoyle's departure takes effect. Ambassadorial nominations require Senate confirmation, and the Athens post — a traditional posting for major donors and political allies — now joins the list of vacancies the administration must fill. Guilfoyle's next move is also unclear: she has said she will contest the allegations, which could keep the dispute in public view well after her resignation.
